subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config surface and changes how security-sensitive tool inheritance works between requester agents and spawned children.

options.title: Sponsor Delegate-Only Config
options.body: Add a documented `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly`-style field with deny-wins precedence, visible diagnostics, and tests for requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Fold Into Per-Spawn Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until the per-spawn tool restriction design also covers requester self-denial and inherited-tool semantics.

options.title: Reject New Config Surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or prompt-level delegation as the supported pattern, accepting that config-level separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Delegate-Only Config
recommendation.body: Add a documented `selfDeny` or `delegateOnly`-style field with deny-wins precedence, visible diagnostics, and tests for requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.
